chunks: And when it is said to them: 'believe in what God has sent down,' they say: 'We believe what was sent to us, and do not believe what has come thereafter,' although it affirms the truth they possess already. Say: 'Why have you then been slaying God's apostles as of old, if you do believe?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Children of Israel reject later prophets despite claiming belief in earlier scriptures?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the concept of *Tahrim al-Tawrat* (blocking the Torah) or the specific rejection of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by those who recognized his attributes in their scriptures. It underscores the inconsistency of claiming belief in divine revelation while historically persecuting the prophets, a theme that resonates with the Shia narrative of the Ahl al-Bayt's suffering at the hands of those who claimed adherence to earlier covenants.
